newsitem.title: USA: N.J. revenue windfall may kill bond sale -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. revenue windfall may kill bond sale -- paper.

text.p: New Jersey lawmakers opposed to a $2.8 billion pension bond deal are expecting new support this week for their argument that the deal is unnecessary -- a surplus that could be as high as $550 million, the Star-Ledger reported Monday.

Treasurer Brian Clymer is scheduled to present the state Legislature with updated revenue figures on Wednesday, and lawmakers said the large expected surplus could be used to eliminate the need for pension bonds.

Gov. Christine Whitman's plan is to sell the bonds to eliminate the state's unfunded pension liability. At the same time, the move would free up nearly $600 million of budget savings by allowing Whitman to avoid the state's annual pension system contribution.

But many lawmakers have balked at the unprecedented size of the bond sale, and state coffers flush with cash are expected to bolster the argument that other methods of balancing the budget are available.
